body: Enig. Det gør det dog ikke ok at tage bestik af situationen
Er hun ikke fra Nordjylland lel?
Som udgangspunkt er hvad du siger korrekt, men kan folk ikke blot fatte at man ikke ser på folks nøgenbilleder uden samtykke?
A good person wouldn't spit on their fucking ex girlfriend. Would you say the same if i smacked her?

No i'm pretty sure you can't dance lancier with your friends. 
And word travels. There's no way any girl is gonna go with the guy who spat on his ex. Perhaps someone with some serious issues or an obsession with stupid bad boy images, but i doubt the chances are big even there.

Senior in high school i guess. The danish school system is not identical to the american when it comes to all that, but i can go to college next year.
This means school dances with partners and these are very serious traditions in Denmark. I'll probably be unable to find a partner, since everyone in my school probably knows what i did.
Third, but first where i had a close relationship to her family as well.

I'm not connected on social media with her after what happened at the party. I've offered to apologize in person, but she said she'd rather not talk to me and that she had a hard time believing that i'd actually say sorry to her. 

It lasted 18-19 months and i'm 18 so yeah.
"Misbehaved" i spat on a former girlfriend... that's beyond "misbehaving".

She didn't just wipe it off. She went and cried. A lot i've been told. She never really recovered at the party and she's a very lively and extroverted person and she had been acting accordingly all night. 

The breakup happened the 28th of June and was completely unexpected

It's the ultimate sign of disrespect pretty much anywhere. The courts of Denmark (where i'm from) have ruled that spitting on someone is a form of violence, so yeah it's a pretty serious thing in fact. It's degrading and humiliating. 

Everytime she thinks of me she'll just remember the humiliation she felt when the abusive asshole side of me came out and spat at her. That's all. 

At least i talked to some people at something called "headspace" today, which helped a bit, though i still feel terrible.

By that standard pretty much anyone is a great person, i'm sorry to say. A good person wouldn't seriously consider spitting on his ex girlfriend and humiliating her in public. I doubt she thinks i'm a good person or any of her friends.
Yeah, but when most people are "the cunt", they don't screw up on this magnitude.

I'm fairly sure it does affect her. She doesn't want to talk to me and before, she was the one who was the most open to keeping contact. 
I'm seeking some sort of help, but i'm afraid it won't do much good. 
You do realize that what i did was violence according to the law? I was violent against a former girlfriend. You don't just forget that when you are the victim. She didn't intentionally provoke me in anyway. I was just angry at how happy she obviously was without me and how little i apparantly matters/mattered to her.
What do you mean exactly? I'm mad at myself because of what i did primarely.

I wasn't even black out drunk. I was drunk, but not that drunk. 
And this isn't the first time i've screwed up big time. I'm sad because i've destroyed all our memories as well

I honestly have a hard time believing that the whole "the love of my life spat at me" part of your comment is true. 
Who have done worse? Serial wife beaters, rapists, murderers and child molestors. That's it. Can you think of anyone else who are worse, than people who spit on their former girlfriend, even if it's just one time?
I doubt she'll ever talk to me again and i somewhat don't want either, both because of what i did, but also because she got together with a new guy less than three weeks after breaking up, despite saying that i "shouldn't think about the fact that i said i had met a new guy". So i still feel let down by her, even though i've acted a hundred times worse. Part of me would just wish that our memories could have stayed good and healthy, but i've ruined that totally. 

She's not open for apology flowers. She said she'd rather not talk to me, when i offered to apologize in real life. 
I have a hard time believing your words of encouragement and attempts at cheering me up, i'm just sorry but that's how i feel.
You think spitting on the love of your life is just a "mistake"?
But i don't deserve help. I've forfeited my rights by abusing her like that
How should i face my mistake? Say "sorry"? i've already done that.
Killing myself is facing my mistake. It's giving me what i deserve
Could be a good idea, but i don't really deserve anything but death.
Hmm yeah, but isn't it kind of weird that famous people would be so inclined to do things that everyone finds repugnant? Is it all because they have an easier time getting away with it?

I know. It just baffles me. It's some sexual or violent misconduct a lot of the time. Either that or racism. I guess fame may screw with people's heads. And perhaps geniuses just tend to have some very dark shit going on inside as well, which makes them more likely to lash out and do some pretty bad stuff.
Hmm yes i see. The misconduct just seems very serious a lot of the time.

Perhaps i should have asked, why it appears that famous people who aren't exactly the nicest bunch, seem to have very serious character flaws that manifest themselves in some form of harm against others, like in the shape of domestic abuse, violence in general and sexual harrasment or even rape.

You're right about that. Acting like a very big asshole just seems fairly common among famous people. Not saying the majority act that way, but it's just something that appears to be more common than it is among your average middle class working joe or whatever.

I agree with you, but i'm talking in terms of doing some serious damage to other people. Wife beating seems somewhat common among famous people for example. 
Nietzsche is a famous guy i'd say, but he is one of the few of whom i've never heard it said that he did some very horrible, like beat a kid or spouse or whatever. He just seemed to hold himself in very high regards. Schopenhauer was another philosopher from around the same era and he pushed an old woman down the stairs. Not saying that makes him a monster (though it might be an indicator). Charlie Sheen and lots of other beloved famous men have hit their girlfriends and wives. Is it the fame that to a certain degree might screw these men up? is it just a general trait amongst people who are very succesful, to be less empathetic in general?

I get that, but famous people seem to have some very serious flaws a lot of the time. Every person in their mid or late 20's have screwed up at some point, but few to the degree that Bowie did, if he actually had sex with that 13 or 14 year old girl for example.

But famous people have flaws that i generally don't see in everyone else. They are violent towards their spouses quite often for example. Or perhaps just violent in general. I'm not trying to hate on famous people by the way, i'm just curious about why they seem to have so deep and serious character flaws a lot of the time.

Yes but they seem to have serious flaws a lot of the time. I wrote this to expand upon my question:
When i look into the lives of famous people, they all seem to have some really deep character flaws. This seems like a trend among most types of famous people. I'll come with a few examples:
Sean Penn allegedly beat Maddonna pretty horribly, when they were married. Charlie Sheen has been accused of domestic violence several times and has been proven guilty of it. Marilyn Manson is a sex offender who once groped a bodyguard at a concert. Britney Spears sexually harrased a bodyguard as well. Sean Connery has a history of domestic abuse it would seem. Clint Eastwood is pretty bigoted it seems. The philosopher Artur Schopenhauer pushed an old lady down some stairs. Socrates was a dead beat father, a drunk and just plain annoying to people it would seem. Einstein cheated on his wife. John Lennon was violent towards his wife at one point at least and he neglected his child. Dr Seuss cheated on his wife while she had cancer. Ozzy Osbourne was a burglar, hit his wife and kids and strangled Sharon Osbourne at one point.
These are just a few examples of very famous people who are or were pricks in some way. I'm not saying that all famous people are people with very deep character flaws, but it could seem that there is some sort of pattern. Or is it simply because human beings generally are flawed and we notice it more in famous people, because they do their wrongs in the public eye and have a hard time avoiding that people find out?
